llm.summary: This is a coherent website-building skill, but its bundled auth, database, payment, and analytics code has security gaps that could put deployed users or transactions at risk.

dimensions.detail: JWT, AI, payment, database, network, KV, and deployment access are proportionate for the advertised full-stack scaffold. However, the actual auth and D1 helper code handles sensitive credentials and payment/order state in unsafe ways for a production-oriented template.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: I found no postinstall hook, hidden installer, or automatic system modification. Scripts are explicit; migration execution requires a command or flag, and the init script is interactive.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill includes broad website-building triggers and can lead to deployment, database migration, payment activation, and secret configuration. It does include user-confirmation checkpoints, but the activation and tool scope are broad for high-impact app generation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is application-level and disclosed: KV sessions, refresh metadata, AI history, analytics counters, localStorage, D1 business records, and cron order transitions. I found no system-level persistence, but users should review retention, analytics, and cron behavior before production use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to scaffold EdgeOne Pages full-stack sites with auth, ecommerce, AI chat, and admin modules, and most artifacts fit that purpose. The concern is that the shipped implementation contradicts several of its own security claims around bcrypt, secure cookies, token handling, and transaction safety.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Treat this as review-required before installing or using for a real site. Do not connect production databases, real payment credentials, or real users until the auth flow, token responses, cookie flags, D1 async handling, payment transaction behavior, and analytics opt-out/feature gating are fixed and tested.
llm.findings:
[TP2] expected: The mixed Chinese and English skill name matches the bilingual EdgeOne website-scaffold purpose; I did not find artifact evidence of a spoofed or visually deceptive tool identifier.
[TP4] expected: Analytics is disclosed in the README, SKILL.md, and templates, and active code sends events to the same-site analytics endpoint backed by KV; the external forwarding path is commented out. The remaining concern is under-scoped automatic collection, not active external exfiltration.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad triggers such as generic website-building phrases are not necessary for the high-impact deployment, payment, and secret-handling capabilities, though the SKILL.md does add confirmation checkpoints.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact claims Edge functions are lightweight and bcrypt belongs in Cloud Functions, but the actual Edge login code has a direct DB branch comparing the password to password_hash as plaintext.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Analytics is presented as optional and opt-out capable, but client startup calls initAnalytics unconditionally and I did not find an implemented feature gate or opt-out check in the inspected code.
[SDI-1] expected: Notification integrations can send data to email, WeChat, DingTalk, or SMS, but they are documented as Layer 2 functionality and appear purpose-aligned for ecommerce/admin notifications.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill asks agents to perform high-impact actions such as deployment, migration, environment variable setup, and payment activation without a machine-readable allowed-tool or permission boundary.
[E1] expected: Outbound AI API calls are expected for the AI chat module and are tied to the declared AI_API_KEY capability; users still need vendor and data-sharing review before production use.
[T09] unexpected: The supplied static scan claim is supported by artifact code: login.js includes plaintext-compatible password verification, returns access and refresh tokens in JSON, and sets auth cookies without the Secure attribute despite security documentation saying otherwise.
[T09] unexpected: The supplied static scan claim is supported by artifact code: cloud-functions/utils/db.js exposes synchronous-looking D1 helpers while many callers use them without await in registration, order, admin, and payment paths, undermining validation and transaction assumptions.
